item.title: Spring Conference Meals Thank You
item.description:
The Spring 2026 Conference Meals on March 12 & 17 successfully provided food for teachers during extra-long workdays at Kramer. Thanks to helpers and donors, there was plenty of food, smooth setup/cleanup, and even leftovers. Teachers posted sweet thank-you notes on refrigerators expressing gratitude. Special thanks to Kramer PTG and numerous volunteers including Andrea Bennett-Kenne, Jessica Brechin, Tomoko Brown, Jennifer Bulanda, and many others. Coordinators: Lois Meade & Tomoko Brown.

item.description:
The Talawanda Community Page provides information about local events and resources. PUSH (People United for Self Help) offers grants to low-income homeowners in the Talawanda School District for critical and emergency home repairs. item.title: Girls on the Run Spring Registration Open
item.description:
Girls on the Run is now accepting registration for grades 4-5 for the Spring 2026 season (March 2 - May 9). The program focuses on building confidence, setting goals, making friends, and healthy habits through physically active games—not just running. Practices meet Monday and Wednesday from 3:45-5:15 PM at Kramer Elementary in Mrs. Story's room 117. Registration is open February 9-22, 2026 at www.gotrcincinnati.org. Contact Erin Story at 513-273-3500 ext. for more information.

item.title: Read At Home Program and Kroger Rewards
item.description:
Read At Home (RAH) is a voluntary program for K-2nd grade students at Kramer Elementary that encourages reading at home. Students record books they've read each week on a record sheet and turn it in for rewards, which alternate between a student-selected book and a small prize.

Kroger Community Rewards: Connect your Kroger Rewards card to Kramer PTG (one nonprofit per account) and Kroger will donate a percentage of your purchases to the PTG. Sign up once at https://www.kroger.com/i/community/community-rewards

item.title: Kramer Free Pantry Available to Students
item.description:
The Kramer Free Pantry is located at the entrance of Kramer and provides free food and hygiene items to all students. Available items include cereal, fruit, vegetables, peanut butter, spaghetti, mac and cheese, soup, shampoo, and toothbrushes. For questions, donations, or suggestions, contact Chelsea Pike, Kramer Social Worker at 513-273-3511 or pikec@talawanda.org.

item.title: Reading Corner Newsletter on Decoding Skills
item.description:
The February Reading Corner Newsletter explains decoding—the foundational reading skill of recognizing letter sounds and blending them to read words. The newsletter provides grade-specific decoding activities for Kindergarten through 3rd grade via Reading Rockets website links, including a video showing how 3rd graders use syllables to decode longer words. Parents can contact Mrs. Geshan (geshanc@talawanda.org), Mrs. Kobermann (kobermanc@talawanda.org), or Mrs. Walters (waltersh@talawanda.org) with questions.

item.title: K-Mart Store Open Every Monday and Friday
item.description:
The K-Mart student store is open every Monday and Friday from when you walk in until the bell rings. It is located on the balcony between 4th and 5th grade classrooms at Kramer Elementary. The store sells fidgets, snacks, and toys with all items priced at one dollar. The next opening is February 9th for 3rd-5th grade students.

item.title: Preschool Lottery Application for 2026/2027
item.description:
Talawanda Preschool is accepting lottery applications for typically developing children for the 2026/2027 school year. Applications must be completed by January 31, 2026, and the lottery will be held on February 13, 2026. Families will be notified of placement or waitlist status after February 13th. Contact Preschool Coordinator Beth Fuechsl at fuechsle@talawanda.org with questions or visit the Preschool Application.

item.title: Principal's Weekly Update from Marshall
item.description:
Principal Mrs. Jones celebrates a successful week at Marshall, highlighting students' strong academic engagement and positive behavior. Students demonstrated respect, responsibility, and readiness to learn through classroom collaboration, peer helping, and supportive friendships. The principal thanks families for reinforcing these values at home and looks forward to another great week.
